entry.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
entry.summary: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.

entry.title: GradFlex: a Gradient-Based Method for Weak Lensing Flexion Measurement
entry.summary: Flexion, the second-order gravitational lensing distortion, probes small-scale mass distribution and complement the cosmic shear measurement. However, its detection is highly challenging due to the faint signal and the contamination arising from the intrinsic galaxy morphology. In this Letter, we present GradFlex, a new method that extracts flexion from the gradient field of galaxy surface brightness distributions without assuming a specific point-spread function model or galaxy morphology. Using surface-brightness conservation, we relate the pre- and post-lensing gradient fields and derive flexion estimators from ensemble-averaged statistics of the corresponding spins. Tests on numerical simulations across diverse galaxy morphologies and multiple noise realizations demonstrate its reliability under realistic observing conditions. Combined with shear measurements, it could tighten constraints on cluster density profiles and enable more detailed studies of substructure than shear alone.

entry.title: Massive quantum divergence on the Cauchy horizon of a black hole
entry.summary: We investigate a quantum {\it massive} scalar field in the interior of a charged and spherically-symmetric (Reissner-Nordström) black hole. We examine the behaviour for varying values of the black hole charge, field mass and coupling constant when the field is in two quantum states: Hartle-Hawking (representing a black hole in thermal equilibrium) and Unruh (representing a black hole evaporating via the emission of Hawking radiation). We show that the vacuum polarization (in both states) generically {\it diverges} on the Cauchy horizon, in stark contrast to what happens for massless fields; also, the angular components of the quantum stress-energy tensor generically {\it diverge} on the Cauchy horizon and, in at least one of the two states, they do so more strongly than for massless fields. Furthermore, we calculate the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $\{u,v\}$. We show that these fluxes in both states on the Cauchy horizon do not generically vanish. This implies, in particular, that in regular, Kruskal coordinates $\{U,V\}$ the ingoing flux diverges like $V^{-2}$ on the Cauchy horizon (where $V=0$). This divergence suggests that its backreaction via the semiclassical Einstein equations would yield a strong singularity, as opposed to its weaker, classical counterpart. Interestingly, there are exceptions, in which the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates vanish: (i) in the extremal limit (where the black hole is maximally charged); (ii) certain fine-tuned regions of parameter space, where the fluxes change sign.

entry.title: Filament-Arm Node Systems (FANS): A new probe of the winding and chirality of the cosmic web
entry.summary: We define Filament-Arm Node Systems (FANS), a new class of cosmic-web objects consisting of multiple filament arms connected to a common node, and use their geometry to construct an object-based test of cosmic chirality. With the cosmic-web node providing a natural reference point, FANS span characteristic scales of ~60 Mpc/h, allowing the coherent winding of their arms around the node to be measured directly. We define cosmic spirality as the amplitude of this winding and handedness as its signed clockwise (CW) or counter-clockwise (CCW) sense. We further introduce an axis-conditioned extrinsic estimator that searches for the projected signature of a coherent three-dimensional axial pattern of the handedness field, corresponding to a preferred axis of winding. Applying these measurements to two distinct SDSS filament reconstructions, and assessing their significance with sign-flip nulls and 27 controlled variations of the FANS construction parameters, we find no significant preference for CW or CCW winding, either globally or around a preferred axis. The data are therefore consistent with parity symmetry, as expected in standard LCDM cosmology. Comparing the lowest- and highest-redshift bins over 0.1<z<0.6, we find that cosmic spirality decreases with cosmic time, a trend that also persists within individual arm-multiplicity classes and may reflect the gravitational straightening of filament arms. These first constraints establish FANS as a new probe of cosmic-web symmetry and large-scale morphology and provide a baseline for future parity tests with the much larger filament samples expected from upcoming surveys.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages, 6 figures. Published in ApJ Letters. Added tests at fixed arm multiplicity and corrected the application of quality cuts in sample selection

entry.title: Cepheid Metallicity in the Leavitt Law (C-MetaLL) survey: X First spectroscopic characterization of Galactic Type II Cepheids and calibration of the Period-Wesenheit-Metallicity relations
entry.summary: Type II Cepheids (T2Cs) are Population II pulsating stars that serve as distance indicators through their period--luminosity relation. Along with RR Lyrae stars and the tip of the red giant branch, they offer an independent route to the Hubble constant, helping assess systematic uncertainties in its determination. We aim to investigate the impact of chemical composition on T2Cs' period--luminosity relations by building a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of Galactic T2Cs with iron and oxygen abundances. We observed 80 Galactic T2Cs with UVES at the ESO Very Large Telescope. For 74 stars, we derived stellar parameters and iron and oxygen abundances through a self-consistent spectroscopic analysis based on equivalent widths of absorption lines. This sample nearly doubles the number of T2Cs with spectroscopic metallicity measurements available in the literature. We used these abundances to test theoretical predictions for the instability strip and, together with $Gaia$ parallaxes, to derive Period--Wesenheit--metallicity (PWZ) relations. In agreement with theoretical predictions, the metallicity coefficient ($γ$) is small and statistically consistent with zero in all relations, ranging from approximately $-0.02$ to $+0.17$ mag dex$^{-1}$. We also estimated distances to 22 Galactic Globular Clusters hosting T2Cs, finding agreement within uncertainties with independent literature estimates. Our results show that metallicity has, at most, a minor impact on T2Cs' pulsation properties and distance scale, supporting their reliability as Population II distance indicators.
entry.arxiv:comment: Article proposed for acceptance in Astronomy & Astrophysics. 12 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables

entry.title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
entry.summary: Karchev et al. (2026) derived a value of H0 by combining the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with SH0ES calibrator Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia; Riess et al. 2022), used to anchor the SN Ia absolute luminosity. The ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset (Rigault et al., 2025) is the largest (O(3000)) SN Ia sample to date obtained with a single telescope. However, as emphasized in the data release, the absolute photometric calibration of the survey has not yet been established to the precision required for cosmological inference. The relative photometric zeropoint offset between the SH0ES and ZTF SN Ia DR2 samples, which is fully degenerate with H0, is therefore unknown and cannot be determined from publicly available data. The photometric corrections introduced in Karchev et al. (2026) do not address this global calibration offset. Consequently, their reported H0 determination is not supported by the available calibration information. We nonetheless share the excitement of pursuing state-of-the-art cosmology with ZTF and are actively working toward the release of a fully calibrated dataset

entry.title: Multi-epoch monitoring of the faint northern component in 3C 84 during 2016-2021
entry.summary: We present the results of multi-epoch very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations of the sub-parsec-scale northern jet component of 3C 84 (known as the N1 component) at 7 mm from 2016 to 2021. The peak position of the N1 component exhibits positional variations of approximately 0.2 mas at a distance of about 2.5 mas from the central radio core (C1) throughout the observation period. Although a linear fit yields a small proper motion of $μ_{\rm{Dec}}=0.054\pm0.019~\rm{mas}~\rm{yr}^{-1}$, corresponding to an apparent velocity of $β_{\rm{app}}=0.062\pm0.021$, this displacement is comparable to the observed positional scatter, and the hypothesis that N1 exhibits systematic motion is not statistically supported. In contrast, the peak flux density varies by approximately a factor of two on timescales of several months. We propose two possible explanations for the observed behavior of N1. One is that N1 is the counterpart of the southern hotspot C3, but its motion has been halted by a collision with a compact and dense cloud along its path; in this case, the flux variability may be caused by changes in the free-free absorption opacity of the non-uniform cloud. The other possibility is that N1 is part of the northern jet that is heavily obscured by foreground free-free absorption and is observed through a gap in the absorbing medium; in this case, the variability may reflect intrinsic changes in the jet and its interaction with a non-uniform ambient medium. These results provide new constraints on the physical origin of N1 and on the circumnuclear environment of 3C 84.
entry.arxiv:comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in PASJ

entry.title: Stochastic dynamics from O(2N) fractional Laplacian vector model and O(N) vector model free energy in finite temperature
entry.summary: We explore O(2N) vector model with fractional Laplacian, $\sqrt{-\nabla^2}$ in $d$-dimension and its Hamiltonian dynamics which is described by a Schrodinger type equation. This equation is a kind of current conservation equation, where one can define a current $j(φ^a)$ of a probability $P(φ^a)$, where $φ^a$ is the O(2N) vector field. Naturally, Gibbs entropy $S=-\int [Dφ^a] P(φ^a)\log P(φ^a)$ can be considered to explore the system. We realize that this Gibbs entropy of the O(2N) vector model with fractional Laplacian is matched with free energy of O(N) vector model at finite temperature, $1/β$ with a deformation, $μ$ in $d$-dimension. The precise map between the stochastic fictitious time $t$ and the inverse temperature $β$ is $β=2t$. Therefore, the temperature dependence of the thermal O(N) vector model can be realized as the dynamics of a time dependent solution satisfying Schrodinger type equation. This free energy is obtained by putting O(N) vector model in $S^1\times \mathbb R_d$, where $S^1$ is thermal circle with its periodicity $β$. To get $d$-dimensional theory, we sum up all possible frequencies on the circle(so called Matsubara frequency summation) which gives $d$-dimensional thermal partition function. We note that the nontrivial $t$-dependence appears beyond classical limit. To take into account quantum effects, we solve the Hamiltonian dynamics by keeping $\hbar$ corrections. The spectral deformation is mediated by a parameter $l$ such that $μ=β^{-1}\log l$ and so we call this $l$-deformation. This is related to the initial boundary condition of the Schrodinger equation. We also note that the two theories are not equivalent to each other and we just check their correspondence at the level of one-loop determinant, i.e. zero point function in the note.

entry.title: Emergent thermal behavior, synchronization, and non-Hermitian phase transitions in driven-dissipative photon condensates
entry.summary: Driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein condensates of photons in optical resonators have been shown theoretically to exist as a long-lived, yet metastable state stabilized by a ghost attractor, despite continuous driving [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 053402 (2025)]. Here we analyze the properties of this metastable condensate as well as the relaxation dynamics into and out of this state by means of the Lindblad master-equation approach, treating the condensate and the equal-time, noncondensed fluctuations on the same footing. Despite its nonequilibrium origin, the quasistationary condensate exhibits thermal behavior in that the order-parameter fluctuations scale with system size as in thermodynamic equilibrium, and the photon-number distribution in multimode resonators is in excellent agreement with a Bose-Einstein distribution. A linear stability analysis further reveals the presence of several exceptional points, resulting in multiple non-Hermitian phase transitions associated with the relaxation dynamics into and out of the metastable condensate. These behaviors reconcile apparently contradictory experimental results.
entry.arxiv:comment: 11 pages, 10 figures. Added multimode thermalization and synchronization

entry.title: Searching for axion-like particles with SPHEREx
entry.summary: We study prospects to detect axion-like particles (ALPs) with the upcoming near-infrared telescope SPHEREx. The signal under investigation is the ALP decay into two photons. Assuming dark matter (DM) to be in the form of ALPs, we analyze the signal from the DM halos of dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Large Magellanic Cloud and the Milky Way. We find that SPHEREx can significantly improve current limits on the axion-photon coupling in the 0.5-3 eV ALP mass range.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. v3: sensitivities corrected, see note added. Conclusions unchanged

entry.title: Gravitational Thermodynamicization of Primordial Black Holes: An RVB Residue Formulation of Thermal Formation and Nonequilibrium Evolution
entry.summary: We establish a controlled, local, and quasi-stationary thermodynamic framework for neutral, nonrotating primordial black holes (PBHs) by combining a local residue prescription with the thermodynamicization of gravitational dynamics. For a nonextremal spherical horizon, we demonstrate that the positive residue of a meromorphic one-form directly determines the inverse Hawking temperature. Applying the first law of thermodynamics recovers the standard Schwarzschild temperature and Bekenstein-Hawking entropy under standard normalization. The resulting entropy defines an off-shell canonical exponent, which reveals that equilibrium thermal production of PBHs is exponentially suppressed in a radiation-dominated universe, thereby confirming that the standard density-perturbation collapse criterion remains the primary formation mechanism. For post-formation evolution, we adopt a detailed-balance mass law, prove the validity of the generalized second law of thermodynamics, and express the evolution dynamics as a free-energy gradient flow where the moving mass acts as an instantaneous evaporation-accretion threshold. Finally, we derive explicit first-order shifts for the temperature, entropy, thermal saddle, and nucleation exponent under small analytic deformations of the residue.

entry.title: Anomalous Low-temperature Magnetotransport in Kagome Metal CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ under Pressure
entry.summary: As a unique kagome superconductor displaying clear signatures of strong electronic correlations, CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$ has drawn much attention. Its rich temperature-pressure phase diagram features intertwined orders including pressure-induced superconductivity and two density-wave-like phases, making it an outstanding platform to explore the complex coexistence and competition of multiple quantum orders. At around 30 K, which we designate as $T_3$, a possible anomaly manifesting as a hump in the resistivity has been observed, yet its nature remains largely unexplored due to limited supporting evidence from other probes. Here, we conducted systematic magnetotransport experiments under hydrostatic pressure to investigate the nature of this anomaly. Our results reveal an abundance of intriguing magnetotransport signatures below $T_3$, including a non-trivial temperature dependence of the Hall coefficient, multi-band characteristics, and pressure-enhanced anomalous-Hall-like effect. These signatures bear resemblance to those observed in many other correlated materials with distinct origins. These findings suggest the possibility of an additional electronic order in CsCr$_3$Sb$_5$, calling for further detailed investigations.

entry.title: FALCON (FERMI-ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN): Cross-matching ALMA Calibrators with Fermi-LAT Blazars
entry.summary: Blazars are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets closely aligned with our line of sight, producing Doppler-boosted emission from radio to gamma rays. Millimeter emission near the synchrotron self-absorption turnover probes compact regions at the jet base, yet large statistical studies in this regime remain limited. We construct the FALCON (FERMI--ALMA Calibrator ObservatioN) catalogue, a millimeter-selected blazar sample by cross-matching the ALMA Calibrator Source Catalogue with the Third Data Release of the Fourth LAT AGN Catalog (4LAC-DR3). After removing duplicates, we obtain 949 unique gamma-ray-associated sources, corresponding to approximately 25 % of the 4LAC-DR3 blazar population. For the subset with available redshift measurements, we compute millimeter and gamma-ray luminosities and find a strong, statistically significant correlation that remains robust after accounting for redshift effects. Fermi-detected blazars exhibit systematically flatter millimeter spectral indices than gamma-ray non-detected ALMA calibrators, while the redshift-controlled luminosity correlation becomes progressively weaker from high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lacs toward flat-spectrum radio quasars. These results indicate an intrinsic connection between millimeter and gamma-ray emission, consistent with a common origin in relativistic jets governed by Doppler boosting and time-averaged jet power.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ

entry.title: Generating entangled polaritonic condensates by pumping with entangled pairs of photons
entry.summary: We investigate the steady state of two single-mode, uniform, spatially separated polaritonic condensates exposed to resonant pumping with entangled pairs of photons in the presence of incoherent exciton reservoirs created by nonresonant optical pumping. We demonstrate the principal possibility of driving the system to an entangled state despite its exposure to noises arising from the excitonic reservoirs and photon leakage through the microcavity mirrors. We estimate the minimum pair-induced polariton influx required to drive the system into a steady state that violates the partial-transpose criterion for entanglement. Furthermore, we trace the evolution of the system after a sudden switch-off of the entangled pumping. Our analysis provides estimates for the entanglement lifetime in a system of two exciton-polariton condensates.

entry.title: Detection of Gravitational Anomaly at Low Acceleration from a Highest-quality Sample of 36 Wide Binaries with Accurate 3D Velocities
entry.summary: We set out to accurately measure gravity in the low-acceleration range $(10^{-11},10^{-9})\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ from 3D motions of isolated wide binary stars. Gaia DR3 provides precise measurements of the four sky-plane components of the 3D relative displacement and velocity ($\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}$) for a system, but not comparably precise line-of-sight (radial) separation and velocity $v_{r}$. Based on our new observations and the public databases/publications, we assemble a sample of 36 nearby (distance $<150$pc) wide binaries in the low-acceleration regime with relatively accurate values of $v_r$. Kinematic contaminants such as undetected stellar companions are well under control using various observational diagnostics such as Gaia's {\tt ruwe} parameter, the color-magnitude diagram, multi-epoch observations of radial velocities, Speckle interferometric follow-up observations, and requiring Hipparcos-Gaia proper motion consistency. For $Γ\equiv \log_{10}\sqrtγ$ with $γ\equiv G/G_{\rm N}$ (where $G$ is a parameter generalizing Newton's constant $G_{\rm N}$), we find $Γ=0.102_{-0.021}^{+0.028}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ ($0.132_{-0.027}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$) giving a gravity boost factor of $γ=1.60_{-0.14}^{+0.24}$, which rules out Newton. This strong anomaly is dominated by two systems (the pairs of HD 189739, HD 189760, and TYC 259-236-1, TYC 259-906-1) that have 3D relative velocities exceeding their estimated Newtonian escape velocities. Without them, we have $Γ=0.042_{-0.024}^{+0.027}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, $0.057_{-0.031}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, and $0.085_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$ for $<10^{-10.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$. Future radial velocity monitoring and Speckle interferometric imaging for larger samples will be useful to refine the present result.
entry.arxiv:comment: 41 pages (main part) + 39 pages (appendix), ApJ, revised (texts and references added on the Bayesian algorithm and independent solar-system results on gravity)

entry.title: A Quantitative Method to Investigate the Spectral Class Time Evolution of Novae
entry.summary: Novae are spectroscopically classified as Fe II or He/N according to the dominance of Fe II, or He and N emission lines in their pre-nebular spectra, while spectra exhibiting both are classified as hybrid. Whereas the spectral class of a nova is known to correlate with its progenitor properties, a recent detailed spectroscopic follow-up of ten novae suggests instead a time evolution from "early He/N" to "Fe II" and to "late He/N". We investigate here this apparent contradiction using a spectroscopic dataset of 26 novae from the Astronomical Ring for Amateur Spectroscopy (ARAS) Database. For this purpose we introduce a quantitative coefficient, $κ$, defined as the ratio of the flux of the Fe II $λ$5169 line to the mean flux of five He and N emission lines, with $κ> 1$ indicating Fe II-dominated spectra and $κ< 1$ indicating He/N-dominated spectra. This coefficient is shown to provide a reliable quantitative tool for tracing nova spectral evolution while reducing biases from incomplete coverage. A significant fraction of the novae in our sample exhibit at least one transition between Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases. The time evolution of $κ$ closely follows their optical light-curves, repeatedly crossing unity in novae exhibiting jitters, which reveal non-monotonic spectral evolution. Since the light-curve shapes and their time-scales depend on intrinsic progenitor properties, particularly white dwarf mass, they also determine the duration of Fe II- and He/N-dominated phases, introducing a bias in spectral classification when it relies on early, sparse spectra.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ (in press)

entry.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
entry.summary: Cooper pairing is a fundamental aspect of superconductivity and results in charge transport with a basic unit of 2e (e is the electron charge). This basic unit can manifest itself as the denominator in the formula for Shapiro steps of ac Josephson effect-nhf/(2e), where h is the Planck constant, f is the ac frequency and n is an integer. Violation of this standard formula may suggest unconventional physics, such as nhf/4e for charge-4e superconductivity. Here, we report discovery of a new sequence of nhf/3e in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions. The microwave frequency/power, temperature, and current annealing dependences of this exotic sequence consistently point to hf/3e as the unit for Shapiro steps, indicating a Josephson tunneling process involving a trio of electrons (3e). This bunching of an odd number of charges distinguishes itself from well-established superconducting processes, which are carried by composite bosons made of an even number of charges. The unusual observations highlight the important interplay between competing charge orders in twisted bilayer systems.

entry.title: High-frequency water megamasers as precision probes of black holes, galaxies and cosmology: A case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer
entry.summary: Water megamasers in the circumnuclear disks of active galactic nuclei are among the most precise probes of supermassive black holes. VLBI imaging of 22 GHz disk masers has provided geometric distances to independently constrain $H_0$, accurate black hole mass measurements, and sub-parsec views of accretion disk geometry. ALMA has opened a new window into water maser transitions in the sub-mm/mm regime, which trace temperatures, densities and disk regions that are inaccessible at 22 GHz, and can be observed at higher spatial resolution and with less free-free absorption. However, current detections are limited to a few bright extragalactic masers in nearby galaxies. We present the case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer - ALMA2040 - that would open a new parameter space for maser studies. We show that a 10-fold increase in line sensitivity and three times longer baselines compared to ALMA would transform sub-mm maser studies from a few bright detections into a population-level probe, delivering black hole masses and geometric distances from sub-mm masers alone, independent of and complementary to 22 GHz measurements. Integrated into a VLBI array, ALMA2040 would resolve maser disks out to $>$160 Mpc, extend maser black hole masses into the largely untested intermediate-mass regime, reveal magnetic field structure in accretion disks through polarization studies, and test systematics in $H_0$ measurements.
entry.arxiv:comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series

entry.title: Thorium and Europium production in the early Galaxy: Implications for nucleocosmochronology
entry.summary: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology, with the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio providing a promising chronometer. We assess the reliability of log(Th/Eu) as an age indicator by testing whether thorium and europium were co-produced in a constant ratio in metal-poor stars, and evaluate the uncertainties affecting stellar ages. We present new Th and Eu abundance measurements for eight TITANS reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. Combining these measurements with homogeneous literature samples, we investigate the behaviour of log(Th/Eu) as a function of metallicity. We derive ages adopting a theoretical initial r-process production ratio and assess the effects of observational uncertainties and sample statistics. At low metallicity, the observed Th/Eu ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity after excluding stars with anomalous actinide abundances, supporting broadly uniform Th and Eu co-production in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are consistent with expectations for an old, metal-poor halo population, although individual uncertainties remain substantial. Higher spectral resolution is needed to improve Th measurements, while combining stars in coeval populations can provide additional statistical gains. Nucleocosmochronology offers an independent approach to dating the oldest stellar populations. Homogeneous samples of coeval stars, particularly in globular clusters, observed with future high-resolution multi-object spectrographs could provide stronger constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.
entry.arxiv:comment: 15 pages, accepted for publication in A&A

entry.title: Spectral Hierarchy of the Cosmic Web
entry.summary: We introduce a spectral hierarchy of cosmic-web classifications obtained by applying simple scale-weighting kernels to the density field before performing a standard eigenvalue-based web classification. This unifies and extends several widely used web definitions within a single framework: the familiar potential/tidal web (large-scale, nonlocal), a curvature-based web (more local, peak- and ridge-sensitive), and additional higher-derivative levels that progressively emphasize smaller-scale structure. Because the classification is built from second derivatives of the filtered field, successive hierarchy levels align naturally with operator families that appear in renormalised bias and effective descriptions of large-scale structure, providing an explicit bridge between cosmic-web environments and long- and short-range nonlocal bias ingredients. We quantify the information content of the hierarchy with a compact statistic: we map each cell to one of four ordered web types (void, sheet, filament, knot), construct a corresponding ``web contrast'' field, and measure its cross-correlation with halos from the AbacusSummit simulation suite on a coarse mesh with $ΔL\simeq 5.5\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$. We find that the hierarchy retains significant tracer-relevant information from very large scales down to the mesh Nyquist limit, with the more local (curvature/higher-derivative) levels dominating toward nonlinear scales. This makes the spectral hierarchy a practical, interpretable conditioning basis for fast mock-galaxy production and field-level modelling, and a flexible tool for studying environment-dependent clustering and assembly bias.

entry.title: Scattering of massless scalar waves by higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
entry.summary: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. We show that at a fixed frequency, the wave cross section diverges in the forward direction as $θ^{-4}$ in any dimension, with a coefficient fixed by the mass, while the steeper classical law $θ^{-(D-2)^{2}/(D-3)}$ appears only at larger angles and higher frequencies. The charge parameter decreases the critical and the glory impact parameters and widens the glory fringes, and in higher dimensions, the glory pattern has fewer and wider fringes and a weaker backward intensity. For the matched configurations studied here, backward intensity and low-frequency absorption provide the clearest differences, while the intermediate-to-high-frequency spectra are close.

entry.title: Constraints on Compact Dark Matter Population from Micro-lensing Effect of Gravitational Wave for the third-generation gravitational Wave Detector
entry.summary: Since the first direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary black-hole merger by the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration, GWs have emerged as a powerful probe of astrophysics and cosmology. If extragalactic compact dark matter (DM) candidates, such as primordial black holes, constitute a non-negligible fraction of the DM component over a broad mass range, they can imprint distinctive microlensing signatures on GW signals. In this work, we develop a framework to infer the population properties of extragalactic compact DM by simulating microlensing GWs in the frequency band of the third-generation ground-based GW detector, the Einstein Telescope, and analyzing them via hierarchical Bayesian inference. For a population described by a power-law mass function, we show that the detection of only several microlensing GW events among $10^4$ binary black-hole coalescences can constrain the compact DMs abundance to the level of $\sim 10^{-3}$. This forecast demonstrates that searching for and identifying microlensing signatures in future GW observations can provide a complementary approach to constraining compact DM scenarios.

entry.title: Photoinduced switching of orbital-selective Mott states
entry.summary: We investigate light-driven inversion of orbital selectivity in a two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model initially in an orbital-selective Mott phase. Using the matrix-product-state we show that tailored pulse excitations drive interorbital charge transfer that nearly reverses the orbital occupations. Single-particle spectral snapshots exhibit changes consistent with an interchange of the localized and itinerant characters of the orbitals. We analyze the relevant one- and two-photon excitation channels and show that chirping around the lower-frequency resonance enhances the transfer. These results establish a microscopic route to reversing orbital selectivity and accessing long-lived nonequilibrium states in multiorbital systems.

entry.title: Chiral superconductivity on a closed Klein bottle: a chirality wall and its Majorana seam spectrum
entry.summary: We study a spinless $π$-flux lattice superconductor whose normal-state momentum-space fundamental domain is a Klein bottle. Within this model, a glide lift and a hidden antiunitary symmetry independently force the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) Chern number to vanish. A diagonal pairing breaks the antiunitary obstruction exactly when its real part is nonzero; this is necessary, not sufficient, for a chiral phase. We derive explicit Pfaffians determining Chern parity and identify three analytic families of gap closings in a real-pairing section. For a chiral state on a closed real-space Klein bottle, the prescribed pairing and gluing produce a $ΔC=2$ chirality wall. A translation-invariant unfolding resolves two co-propagating Majorana branches. Their finite-size levels depend on circumference and holonomy; the near-zero pair is lifted at first order by allowed local seam perturbations. A cut-cylinder control has the same low-energy channel count, so gluing reconnects existing gapless content. We also distinguish literal gluing from deck projection: particle--hole symmetry exchanges the deck eigenblocks, precluding their interpretation as independent BdG quotient Hamiltonians. Finite odd-frequency correlations track holonomy and local splitting, while cylinder and ordinary-wall controls show that their presence is not specific to Klein gluing. The contribution is a model-specific account of pairing compatibility, closed-surface seam spectra and finite correlations. The energy cost is evaluated for a fixed pairing background; neither a protected zero mode nor a self-consistent wall solution is claimed.
entry.arxiv:comment: 33 pages (23-page main text and 10-page supplement), 17 figures. Adds finite odd-frequency analysis and reproducibility review. Reproducibility archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23967897

entry.title: Emulating the complex galactic-scale orbital dynamics of LISA massive black hole pairs with normalizing flows
entry.summary: Massive black hole (MBH) pairs, formed in galaxy mergers, may coalesce in a burst of gravitational waves (GWs). Estimating the coalescence time-scales and rates is a long-standing astrophysical problem, essential to inform predictions for future GW detectors such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but remains challenging: MBH orbital decay in realistic galactic environments is complex and stochastic, and non-axisymmetric structures such as stellar bars can perturb MBH pair dynamics, delaying or accelerating binary formation and undermining the assumption that dynamical friction alone sets the inspiral duration. Capturing this evolution requires simulations too expensive to run at population scale. Here we present an artificial intelligence framework that emulates the galactic-scale orbital decay of an inspiralling MBH using conditional normalizing flows trained on a large suite of semi-analytical orbital integrations. Our model captures the evolution of secondary MBHs orbiting within multi-component galactic merger remnants featuring rotating stellar discs and bars, across a broad range of MBH masses, orbital configurations, and bar properties. The trained emulator reproduces the simulations' decay-time distributions while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude. For the first time, we apply this model to galaxy populations drawn from a cosmological simulation, exploiting morphological information on barred and non-barred galaxies to infer MBH binary formation time-scales across cosmic time. Our results show that stellar bars can alter the distribution of MBH binary formation times. More broadly, this demonstrates how simulation-based, surrogate machine learning emulators can unlock a class of astrophysical problems where the physics is well understood system-by-system but intractable at scale.

entry.title: Discovery of the redback pulsar PSR J2053+6905 and multi-epoch optical observations of the system
entry.summary: Using the Green Bank Telescope, we discovered the 1.68-ms binary pulsar PSR J2053+6905. The discovery resulted from a targeted search for radio pulsations from a redback candidate, previously identified through optical and X-ray observations and spatially coincident with the $γ$-ray source 4FGL J2054.2+6904. We report the first results from the pulsar timing, including the spin period, dispersion measure, precisely measured Keplerian binary parameters, and the pulsar mass function. We also found potential evidence of scintillation and long radio eclipses. To constrain the system parameters, we performed multi-epoch time-series photometric observations using the 2.1-m telescope at the Observatorio Astronómico Nacional on the Sierra San Pedro Mártir (Mexico) and the 1.5-m telescope of the Maidanak Astronomical Observatory (Uzbekistan), complemented by time-series optical spectroscopy with the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias. The optical light curves revealed a pronounced asymmetry, as well as significant long-term variations. From the spectra, we derived a radial velocity curve semi-amplitude $K = 337(4)$ km s$^{-1}$. Combining it with the pulsar mass function, we constrained the ratio of pulsar and companion masses to $M_{\rm p}/M_{\rm c} = 7.05(8)$. By fitting the stable segments of the light curves with a symmetric direct heating model, we derived constraints on the component masses ($M_{\rm p} \approx 2.1\ {\rm M}_\odot$ and $M_{\rm c} \approx 0.3\ {\rm M}_\odot$), the Roche lobe filling factor, and the companion's day- and night-side temperatures. The long-term evolution of the light curve profiles is likely driven by the dissipation or migration of a cold stellar spot.

entry.title: A Brief Review on the Statistical Properties of Fast Radio Bursts
entry.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin, whose emission mechanisms and progenitors remain unresolved. Statistical analyses of the rapidly growing samples provide a promising means to constrain the underlying physics. In this review, we synthesize the statistical properties derived from current FRB catalogs, encompassing constraints on dispersion measure, redshift, energy/luminosity functions, repetition rate, and host-galaxy demographics. For repeating FRBs, we examine the statistics of energy, fluence/flux, waiting time, and discuss time-series analyses that reveal memory effects and chaotic dynamics. We further discuss the observational discovery and theoretical interpretation of periodic activity, and survey polarization properties that probe the magneto-ionic environments of FRB sources. Throughout, we emphasize robust empirical trends, account for observational biases and selection effects, and outline outstanding open questions regarding the physical origin of these enigmatic bursts.

entry.title: Ground-state properties of uniaxial magnetic model for antiferromagnetic 1/1 periodic approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals
entry.summary: The ground-state properties of the uniaxial magnetic model in the 1/1 periodic approximant to the icosahedral quasicrystal with antiferromagnetic interactions for the nearest-neighbor bond $J_1$ and the next-nearest-neighbor bond $J_2$ are analyzed theoretically. By performing numerically-exact calculation, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram for the interaction strength $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy defined within the mirror plane reflecting the effect of the crystalline electric field. We have discovered non-collinear magnetic structures, whose magnetic space groups are identified as the antiferromagnetic orders $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$ and $R_{\rm R}\bar{3}$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(111)$ as well as the antiferromagnetic orders $Im'm'm'$ and $R\bar{3}'$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(000)$ and the ferrimagnetic orders $Im'm'2$, $I2'2'2$, $P2'/m'$, and $P\bar{1}$. By analyzing each ground state with degeneracy, we have revealed the magnetic as well as topological properties, which are useful to analyze experimental observations of rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants considering the effect of magnetic domains.

entry.title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
entry.summary: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory. Here we combine the truncated Wigner approximation with an asymptotic analysis, and show that this locking is produced by a slowly varying density profile through a universal mechanism, whereby the relative phase near the density maximum drifts towards zero. We show that this drift is already present in the linearised theory and its timescale is determined by the density curvature alone, while it is independent of the tunnel coupling. Rescaling time by the relaxation time scale collapses the dynamics for different system sizes and density profiles, while non-linearity suppresses the excitation returning from the edges.

entry.title: Planckian dissipation from classical hydrodynamics
entry.summary: Hydrodynamics describes the long-time, long-distance dynamics of interacting quantum systems by classical equations, yet at low temperature quantum fluctuations might eventually invalidate this classical picture. Here we ask what it takes for a quantum system to sustain a consistently classical hydrodynamic description. Our starting point is the quantum fluctuation-dissipation theorem which, when read in the time domain, acts as a blurring of the fine details of correlation functions on a Planckian time-scale. We analyse how this blurring interacts with the diffusive large-deviation form of correlators assuming the existence of a hydrodynamic light cone velocity, and show that the interior of the cone splits into a classical region, where correlation and response satisfy the classical fluctuation-dissipation relation, and a quantum region, where they deviate sharply from it. We illustrate the mechanism on three phenomenological hydrodynamic equations - diffusion, telegraph and diffusive-telegraph. Preserving a finite classical region as the temperature is lowered forces the current relaxation rate to be bounded from above by the Planckian rate. This bound connects to bounds on diffusivity, equilibration time and shear viscosity. In this way, a Planckian bound on dissipation emerges not as a quantum constraint on microscopic dynamics, but as the price a system pays to remain describable by classical hydrodynamics down to low temperatures.

entry.title: A two-phase model of galaxy formation: IV. Seeding and growing supermassive black holes in dark matter halos
entry.summary: We present a theoretical framework for seeding and growing supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dark matter halos along their assembly histories. Seeds are bred out of Pop-III stars formed during the first collapse of pristine gas in mini-halos that have reached the ${\rm H}_2$-cooling limit, modulated by UV radiation from star formation and dynamical heating from fast halo assembly. Such breeding persists until the enrichment of the intergalactic medium (IGM) enables Pop-II stars to form. Post-seeding growth of black holes (BHs) is driven by distinct channels, starting with episodic super-Eddington accretion associated with nuclear bursts induced by global disturbances of galaxies, followed by sustained sub-Eddington accretion via capturing sub-clouds formed in self-gravitating gas clouds (SGCs) in halos of fast assembly, and ending with merger-dominated, quiescent growth. We implement the model in subhalo merger trees to build a coherent framework to follow SMBH-galaxy-halo co-evolution across the whole history and structural hierarchy. BH seeds are bred with a broad mass spectrum of $M_{\rm BH} = 10$--$10^5\,{\rm M}_\odot$ at $z \approx 20$--$30$ in mini-halos with masses of $10^5$--$10^8\,{\rm M}_\odot$. Nuclear bursts provide the key condition for seeds to grow into SMBHs. The $M_{\rm BH}$-$M_*$ relation is a multi-piece, redshift-dependent function shaped by the interplay among different growth channels. Our model predictions are broadly consistent with existing observations; in particular, a population of BHs reminiscent of `little red dots' (LRDs) discovered by JWST naturally results from the seeding and growing processes. Potential future tests of the model are discussed.

entry.title: Majorana corner modes and tunable braiding in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure
entry.summary: Zeeman fields are usually required for realizing and manipulating Majorana corner modes at the cost of suppressed superconducting pairing. Altermagnetism offers a new route toward realizing Majorana corner modes under zero net external magnetic fields. Here we propose a theoretical scheme to host Majorana corner modes in a honeycomb-lattice altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure. In contrast to previous studies on square lattices, altermagnetism yields distinct effective low-energy edge masses on various inequivalent edges of the honeycomb lattice. Within a low-energy edge-theory framework, we establish the conditions under which Majorana corner modes emerge for both bearded and zigzag edge terminations. We further explicitly construct a complete set of Clifford gates by tuning the altermagnetic anisotropy and chemical potential of the heterostructure. Our results provide a promising platform for the realization and manipulation of Majorana corner modes.

entry.title: Exact and Near-Exact Inverse Renormalization Group with Constrained Monte Carlo
entry.summary: We establish conditions for exactness of the inverse renormalization group via constrained Markov processes, a class of Monte Carlo simulations which sample the degrees of freedom within a block on a fine lattice under the constraint that they remain consistent with the corresponding degree of freedom on the coarse lattice according to a forward renormalization group transformation. We show analytically, for an arbitrary transformation, that constrained Markov processes correspond to an exact inversion of the renormalization group at the fixed point action, and to a near-exact inversion in the vicinity of the fixed point. We then optimize renormalization group transformations directly on inversely renormalized configurations to effectively map the action onto itself and ensure computational stability in the generation of configurations for high-dimensional systems. Starting from a set of uncorrelated configurations for the three-dimensional $φ^{4}$ quantum field theory at lattice volume $V=16^{3}$, we invert the renormalization group with constrained Monte Carlo to construct a set of uncorrelated, near-equilibrium configurations for $V=128^{3}$ and extract two critical exponents of the system. The inversion exhibits no critical slowing down, with dynamic critical exponent $z=0.03(2)$.

entry.title: Topological Characterization of Adinkra Heights
entry.summary: Adinkras are highly structured bipartite graphs that encapsulate 1D supersymmetry representations. We classify hypercube Adinkra heights with one, two, three or four edge colors using a graph-theoretic notion of equivalence. For the 990 distinct height functions in the case of four edge colors, we show that these classes match modified twisted character classes bijectively and provide a finer classification than spectral Height Yielding Matrix Numbers (HYMNs). We also relate our classification to the physics of the two-dimensional chiral and twisted chiral supermultiplets.

entry.title: Quantum action for heterotic string field theory with quantum L-infinity structure
entry.summary: We construct a quantum action for heterotic string field theory that satisfies the quantum Batalin-Vilkovisky equation. Assuming a triangulation of the bosonic moduli space, the prescription for inserting picture-changing operators is determined based on a quantum L-infinity structure. After concretely constructing some of the lower-order interactions, we propose a general prescription, which generalizes that for constructing the classical interactions governed by a classical L-infinity structure. Assuming it does not suffer from spurious poles, all quantum interactions are determined by iteratively solving differential equations and transforming the solutions via IBL-infinity-transfer. To demonstrate the consistency of our prescription, we compute the one-loop two-point functions (modulo the spurious pole issue) and show that they agree with those in the first-quantized formulation.

entry.title: Inflation, Cosmic Perturbations and Non-Gaussianities
entry.summary: We review the theory of inflationary perturbations. Perturbations at both linear and nonlinear orders are reviewed. We also review a variety of inflation models, emphasizing their signatures on cosmic perturbations.

entry.title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
entry.summary: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

entry.title: Fermi-volume anomaly in quartet condensates
entry.summary: We investigate the relation between density and Fermi volume in a four-component Fermi system with quartet order. For a regular zero-temperature branch without pair order, we express the correction to the Fermi-volume count in terms of the response of the Luttinger-Ward functional to a phase winding of the quartet source. Its leading term is a weighted difference between four-particle and four-hole states. For a Gaussian vertex and parabolic dispersion, we find that the correction expands the Fermi volume in one dimension and contracts it in three dimensions in the parameter range studied. The sign in two dimensions depends on the momentum cutoff. We solve the one-dimensional Dyson equation at fixed density and compare the counting correction obtained from the Fermi points with that evaluated from the dressed spectra at low temperature. At fixed quartet amplitude and peak normalization of the vertex, the correction depends strongly on the vertex width, whereas the fermionic entropy changes little. We also examine the linear pairing response, which can limit the continuation of the unpaired branch to zero temperature.

entry.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
entry.summary: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

entry.title: Rational Orbits and Gravitational-Wave Signatures around a Horndeski Black Hole
entry.summary: We study equatorial timelike geodesics and associated gravitational-wave (GW) emission for a static Horndeski black hole with secondary scalar hair, characterized by an effective pressure parameter $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Using the rational-orbit taxonomy $(z,w,v)$, we analyze the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), marginally bound orbit (MBO), and periodic bound orbits. We find that increasing $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$ systematically shifts orbital radii outward and modifies the rational parameter $q$. Within the test-particle and quadrupole approximations, we estimate GW signals from an extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) system at a luminosity distance of $D_L=8000\,\mathrm{pc}$. The characteristic strains reach $\sim10^{-18}$ in the mHz band, partially overlapping the nominal LISA sensitivity range. These results demonstrate that Horndeski corrections systematically alter strong-field orbital dynamics and GW spectra, offering a phenomenological probe of deviations from general relativity.

entry.title: Dissipative hydrodynamic actions and horizon symmetries in gravity
entry.summary: We give a prescription to compute a dissipative action describing the large-scale thermal stress tensor dynamics of a holographic quantum field theory dual to AdS$_4$ gravity, in the context of the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Our prescription is valid to quadratic order in perturbations about the thermal equilibrium state. The hydrodynamical degrees of freedom of this action are realised in gravity as relative diffeomorphisms between the black hole horizon and the two asymptotic boundaries of the Crossley-Glorioso-Liu contour. We explicitly compute the action to first order in derivatives, and confirm it correctly reproduces the known hydrodynamic Green's functions. Our prescription requires a choice of horizon boundary conditions for the metric. We study the horizon symmetries that preserve these, and their relation to conjectured hydrodynamic symmetries responsible for many-body quantum chaos.

entry.title: The Influence of the Inclination of the Accretion Disk in Black Hole X-Ray Binaries on the Energy Spectrum Characteristics
entry.summary: During the ascending and descending phases of some black hole X-ray binaries(BH XRBs), it was found that the X-ray Eddington ratio ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $) and the photon spectral index $Γ$ had an anticorrelation when the X-ray Eddington ratio was less than a specific value, and a positive correlation when it was greater than that value. Moreover, the cross points of the anticorrelation and positive correlation are different for different BH XRBs ($ L_{X-ray(3-25keV)}/L_{Edd} $ of cross point is between $ 0.1 \% $ and $ 10\% $). The reason why the cross points are different for different BH XRBs were still uncertain. So we processed the light curve and energy spectrum of 15 outbursts of eight BH XRBs during their descending phases. We found that for the same BH XRB, the values of the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point are basically consistent for different outburst times. However, for different BH XRBs, there is a positive linear correlation between the X-ray Eddington ratio at the cross point and the cosine of the accretion disk inclination. Therefore, We think that the geometric effect of the inclination has a significant impact on the evolution of the energy spectrum of the BH XRBs.

entry.title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
entry.summary: A coupling of photons to the cosmic neutrino asymmetry current has been proposed to explain the hinted isotropic rotation of CMB polarization. Gauge invariant UV completions require a Kalb-Ramond field that is exactly dual to a massless axion. We show that, in this case, the product of the axion-photon coupling and the axion-neutrino current coupling is fixed by the signal, $g_{aγ}/f_\ell=1/Λ_*^2$ with $Λ_*\simeq10$ TeV. Using $SU(2)_L$ gauge invariance we show that the dual axion couples to electrons as $g_{aγ}g_{ae}=m_e/Λ_*^2\simeq5\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. This value is excluded by the measured electron magnetic moment combined with light-shining-through-a-wall searches, as well as by stellar evolution. Conserved anomaly-free currents may evade these bounds, but then either a contact interaction among SM fermions excludes the model, or the relic neutrinos decouple from the signal. We conclude that cosmic neutrinos cannot induce a birefringence signal.

entry.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
entry.summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

entry.title: Spinning compact object and chaos in galactic centres
entry.summary: Galactic centres are extremely complex environments, consisting primarily of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) surrounded by asymmetric mass distributions such as nuclear star clusters (NSC) and molecular gas, which form disks or halos. Together these components exert a gravitational field which, combined with relativistic corrections from the spin of the SMBH, generates strongly nonlinear dynamics and chaotic orbits. We model this region using a multipolar expansion potential, in which the central compact object is represented by the Artemova-Björnsson-Novikov pseudo-Newtonian potential, which mimics the spin dependence of a Kerr-like BH. The surrounding halo is modelled as an axisymmetric, shell-like mass distribution expanded to dipole order to induce asymmetry. Previous works have mostly quantified the chaos caused by the BH spin and dipole moment using Poincaré sections, SALI and other chaos indicators. In this study, we incorporate stability analysis and Newton-Raphson basins of convergence to provide a global view of the dynamics of the system. Stability analysis around fixed points gives deeper insight into the local behaviour, while basins of convergence show sensitivity to initial conditions and reveal fractal boundaries. Our results show that the BH spin substantially reshapes the equilibrium landscape. Depending on its magnitude, it can either intensify the chaos induced by the halo asymmetry or simplify the phase space. These results improve our understanding of how relativistic spin effects and multipole moments collectively affect particle motion in galactic centres.

entry.title: ADE Quiver Duality Proposals: Graph Classification and Nodewise Realizations
entry.summary: We use the large-$N$ index strategy to find new quiver dualities in four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ quiver gauge theories. We study gauge quivers with or without an adjoint field at each gauge node, and bifundamental matter between selected nodes with fixed $R$-charges. Imposing the finite-meson condition restricts the allowed gauge graphs to finite ADE diagrams and leads to a new simultaneous duality for ADE quivers. We present an explicit superpotential that produces a uniform classical meson spectrum consistent with the large-$N$ index approach's prediction. We then relate the simultaneous rank transformation to the longest element of the ADE Weyl group, whose reduced expressions organize nodewise duality sequences realizing the simultaneous ADE duality. Realizing the simultaneous ADE duality through such nodewise sequences offers a finite-$N$ consistency check beyond the large-$N$ index construction. Moreover, we realize the simultaneous ADE duality as a sequence of subquiver simultaneous dualities.
